clue.text: One with great expectations…

parts.note: surface reading: Pip, the hero of Dickens's novel Great Expectations
setter's reading: someone who habitually expects things to turn out well

explanation.surface: A nod to Pip, the boy with great expectations in Dickens, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital-free 'great expectations' still calls Dickens to mind; the answer is just a hopeful person. The trailing dots run the sentence on into 5 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who always looks on the bright side expects good outcomes, and so has great hopes of the future.

clue.text: Resistance shown to official communications?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: units of electrical resistance
second meaning: the initials stamped on British government mail, On Her Majesty's Service

explanation.surface: Officials meet opposition to their memos.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as a stretch: the initials marked official letters rather than naming them.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the unit of electrical resistance, and the same letters were the franking on UK government envelopes.

clue.text: Appearing to right a wrong

parts.note: taken as written
RT is a standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone seems to be setting an injustice straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to right a wrong' is the idiom of putting things straight; here right is only an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tort is a civil wrong in law, a harm for which damages can be claimed.

clue.text: Anguish of Margaret, on edge…

parts.note: Meg is a pet form of Margaret
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher, nervous and on edge, suffers torment as the clue runs on into 4 down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, A on B puts A above B. Megrim is an old word for a migraine or low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Megrim is an archaic term for a severe headache or depression, both forms of distress.

clue.text: … over leadership division?

parts.note: surface reading: Margaret Thatcher anguished over a split in her party's leadership in 1990
setter's reading: the head is the part that leads, and division is a split, so this is a severe headache

explanation.surface: Following on from 3 down: Margaret is on edge over a leadership challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: Published in March 1990, months before Thatcher was ousted. A splitting head is everyday speech for a pounding headache.
explanation.definitionFit: A splitting head is a violent headache, the kind of pain that feels like the skull cracking.

clue.text: … managed to find some, but not all the price of freedom

indicators.note: taking only part of the word, not all of it, means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: ran a business means managed it
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: Following on from 1 across: the hopeful one managed to scrape together some, but not all, of what freedom costs.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is the sum demanded to release a captive, literally what their freedom costs.

clue.text: Every type of lads link up together

indicators.note: things mixed up together lose their order and are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of lads and link, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Boys of every kind join hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'link up' looks like a phrasal verb, but up belongs to the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: All kinds of things means things of every variety, the same as every type of.

clue.text: Dramatist is ill-bred, held together with twine

indicators.note: one thing held inside another is enclosed by it

parts.note: twine is a strong string

indicators.note: ill means badly, so the word that follows is made badly, out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A playwright of poor breeding is held together with string.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-bred' looks like a single word meaning rude; the hyphen hides the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: August Strindberg was a Swedish playwright, author of Miss Julie and The Father.

clue.text: Diplomacy about Tory leadership — it's a thought

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: mediation is diplomatic go-between work

indicators.note: leadership is the leading position, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Tory

explanation.surface: A political musing on whether diplomacy surrounds the Tory leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: Meditation is deep reflection or contemplation, a sustained thought on a subject.

clue.text: Flowers make girl so mad

indicators.note: to make something is to build it anew, so these letters are built into a fresh order

parts.note: the letters of girl, so and mad, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's gift of flowers drives a girl to distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' looks like the obvious signal to rearrange, but it is part of the letters; 'make' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: Marigolds are common orange or yellow garden blooms of the daisy family.

clue.text: Thus one not in orders withdraws from worship to work in the community

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

indicators.note: withdrawing is drawing back, so the word for a non-cleric runs backwards

parts.note: laic means lay, one not ordained into holy orders
a church service is an act of worship

explanation.surface: A layman stops attending church in order to do good works locally.
explanation.walkthrough: Holy orders are the ranks of the clergy, so someone not in orders is a layman.
explanation.definitionFit: Social service is welfare work done for the benefit of the community.

clue.text: Ghastly student has free turn first

indicators.note: first tells us the word for a turn comes ahead of the word for free, not after it

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car
a U-turn, so U stands for a turn
to rid someone of a thing is to free them of it

explanation.surface: A dreadful student gets a free turn ahead of everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'free turn' as one phrase and it misleads; the words split, and 'first' moves the turn ahead of free.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid describes something shocking or gruesome, so it shares the horrible sense of ghastly.

clue.text: The fruit of tuition chaps get free

indicators.note: letters that get free break loose from their order and settle in a new one

parts.note: the letters of tuition and chaps, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Pupils reaping the rewards of their education are let out of school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The fruit of tuition' reads as one idiom for learning; only 'The fruit' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistachio nut is the edible kernel of a tree, and botanically a nut counts as a fruit.

clue.text: Dance for joy at relaxation of endless Puritan diet

indicators.note: a relaxation loosens things up, so these letters are loosened into a new order
with no end, the word that follows loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written, then cut short
taken as written

explanation.surface: Celebrating as a strict Puritan diet is finally eased.
explanation.walkthrough: Tripudiate is a rare word, from the Latin for a ritual dance; the anagram is the way in.
explanation.definitionFit: To tripudiate is to leap or dance in exultation, a rare literary word for jubilant dancing.

clue.text: Providing vessel for use in trawling

indicators.note: something for use in another thing is put inside it

parts.note: trawling is fishing with a dragged net
an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: Supplying a boat to be used for trawling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' and 'trawling' suggest a fishing boat; the vessel is a vase.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish is to supply or equip, so furnishing means providing.

clue.text: Reprobate has nothing to repent about

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is wrapped around the other

parts.note: to rue a deed is to regret or repent of it
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A scoundrel who feels no remorse about anything he has done.
explanation.definitionFit: A roué is a debauched man given to vice, which makes him a reprobate.

clue.text: Share the blame for ten bad pieces at Verdi opera

parts.note: Aida is Verdi's opera set in ancient Egypt

indicators.note: in pieces, these words are broken up and put back together differently

parts.note: the letters of ten and bad, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten bad performances of a Verdi opera, and everyone involved must take some of the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: The opera comes first in the answer although it is last in the clue: 'at' places the jumbled pieces beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid and abet is the legal phrase for helping a wrongdoer, which makes one an accomplice sharing the guilt.

clue.text: Guy joins plot with resounding consequence

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, like the adjective answer

parts.note: a plot is a scheme or plan
a guy is a man, a gent

explanation.surface: Guy Fawkes joins the Gunpowder Plot, which ends with a bang.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy and plot call up Guy Fawkes and the Gunpowder Plot, whose consequence would have been an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a sound that is loud and reverberating, often with a mournful ring.

clue.text: Writer with nothing on record is model authority on sentences

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
O looks like zero
a log is a written record, as a ship's log
taken as written
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A writer with nothing published is held up as the ideal judge of sentence construction.
explanation.walkthrough: The grammar picture is the trap: the sentences are prison terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A penologist studies punishment and prison management, so is an expert on the sentences courts hand down.

clue.text: Transport has no place in Moravia

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former UK national railway
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that there is nowhere for transport in Moravia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no place' looks like one phrase; 'no' is a piece and 'place in Moravia' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Brno is the chief city of Moravia, the eastern region of the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Law requires no model for a sculpture

indicators.note: requiring none of something means doing without it, so it is taken out

parts.note: a statute is a written law
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A rule that a sculptor need not use a model.
explanation.walkthrough: The sculptor's model is not a sitter: it is the T removed from the law.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a carved or cast figure, a kind of sculpture.

clue.text: Fall apart — it is red agent's work

indicators.note: the letters are worked over, made into something new

parts.note: the letters of these four words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A communist spy's sabotage makes the whole thing collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: A red agent is a Soviet spy, which fits the theme of things falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that disintegrates breaks into fragments, which is exactly falling to pieces.

clue.text: Noxious gas gets mother into such a state

parts.note: CO is the chemical formula for carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Poisonous fumes leave a mother in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the surface: carbon monoxide poisoning can put someone into exactly this state.
explanation.definitionFit: A coma is a state of deep unconsciousness, the sort carbon monoxide poisoning can cause.

clue.text: Like a pagan deity, in sound but no action

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjective: having no action, doing nothing

indicators.note: in sound means judged by how the word is pronounced, not written

parts.note: an idol is the image of a pagan god

explanation.surface: A heathen god's image: impressive to hear of, but it never does anything.
explanation.walkthrough: An idol is a false god, and idle sounds the same; 'in sound but no action' also mocks an idol that cannot act.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means inactive or unoccupied, the state of having nothing going on.

clue.text: Chemical found in an excavation

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, A
a mine is a hole dug for ore

explanation.surface: A chemical substance turns up at a dig site.
explanation.definitionFit: An amine is an organic compound derived from ammonia, a class of chemical compound.

clue.text: Debtor, in the event of proverbial company being overdrawn, may keep afloat or go to the bank

definitions.text: may keep afloat or go to the bank
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a noun: something that may float or wash ashore

parts.note: DR is the bookkeeping abbreviation for debtor
if means in the event that
the proverb says two's company, three's a crowd
OD is the banking abbreviation for overdrawn

explanation.surface: A financial warning: a debtor whose account goes overdrawn may stay afloat or have to visit the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The money words all play double: afloat and the bank belong to a river, where floating wood drifts or is washed up on the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Driftwood is timber that floats on water and is eventually washed up on a shore or riverbank.

clue.text: Boats' cruise, we hear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: racing shells rowed by eight oarsmen
second meaning: said out loud this is crews, and a rowing crew of eight takes the same name

explanation.surface: A boating trip, described as a sea cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: Cruise is pronounced like crews, and an eight is both the racing boat and the crew that rows it.
explanation.definitionFit: In rowing, an eight names both the long racing shell and the team of eight oarsmen in it.

clue.text: Got together and noshed — er, dined

definitions.note: past tense, while the answer is the present-tense verb

parts.note: noshed means ate, or fed
taken as written, the sound of hesitation
to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: People met up and had a bite, er, dinner, correcting the slangy word mid-sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is past tense but the answer is present; the setter has stretched the tense.
explanation.definitionFit: To federate is to unite separate states or bodies into one union, joining together.
